The pool opened 2026-07-10; **in its first 5.2 days it consumed 17.8% of the annual budget**.

- Burn rate to date: **372.9 QPU-s/day** — **12.6× the straight-line guide** (10,800 ÷ 365 = 29.6 s/day).

- To fit the 12-month window, the remaining budget must average **≤ 24.7 s/day** for ~360 days.

**Read**: a front-loaded burst, not steady-state — see the narrative below the markers for which arc
drove it. Steer back toward the 900 s/mo straight-line pace between sprints (C4536 policy).

## Narrative — what drove the current burst (hand-maintained)

The drawdown pool's front-loaded 5-day burn is the **F106→F118 arc** + the **Exp135/136/137/138b
trust-ladder** + **F112's 3-device** work, all flown inside that window. The 98s `d9ansru6…` job is
Exp137 (**F117**, the 1SDI certified-randomness capstone). Whisper's adversarial-audit cycles
(C4713–C4718) are **QPU-free** Monte-Carlo — zero pool draw. Cadence falls off naturally as the arc
consolidates; the pace flag is a signal to steer by, not an alarm (Creator: "budget is OK … I will
add more time when possible if it runs out").

## Method & caveats
- **check_usage.py** → authoritative pool state (consumed/limit/window) from `instances/usage`.
  Run before any large job.
- **qpu_usage_tally.py** → per-job / per-backend / per-month breakdown; enumerates all jobs the
  current credentials expose (drawdown-era instance).
- **qpu_spend_refresh.py** → wraps both, computes the pace, and rewrites the AUTO block above.
- "usage" = IBM-billed **execution** QPU-seconds (per-job overhead in, queue time out).
  **Wall-clock overestimates QPU time** (Creator's standing note) — never infer depletion from wall
  time or queue duration.
- The old-account 600s is documentation-based (not re-queryable). Cancelled/zero-usage jobs excluded.
- The pre-drawdown and drawdown eras are **additive, not overlapping**: the C4535 tally captured
  pre-reset July jobs; the pool's `usage_consumed` (the AUTO block above) counts only jobs after the
  2026-07-10 02:16 reset.
